subject: Rackside site intake: node profiles, local NVMe topology & retention constraints
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@rackside.io>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Rackside site intake: node profiles, local NVMe topology & retention constraints

Hi Sarah — great to meet you on the call earlier. Per our intake checklist I wanted to capture a few concrete items so we can size the on‑prem cluster and propose node pools and storage layout. Could you confirm the following from your side?

- Number of GPU hosts available in Rack A and Rack B (if you have exact host SKUs even better).
- Are any hosts behind an additional rack-level firewall/NAT?
- Do you have local NVMe on each host, and if so, are those SSDs dedicated to tenant workloads or shared with host-local caching?
- Retention requirement for logs and model artifacts (e.g., 30d / 90d / 1yr) and whether you need WORM controls.

I've attached a short inventory CSV template and a simple NVMe topology sketch to fill out. Once we have these, Neha and Priyom will draft a proposed node mix (control plane hosts, GPU worker pools with local NVMe ephemeral vs persistent PVCs, and a small blob-store plan).

Goal: deliver a recommended node-pool + storage baseline and a preflight checklist by next Friday (2026-10-08).

Thanks,
Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@rackside.io>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@rackside.io
Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rackside site intake: node profiles, local NVMe topology & retention constraints

Hi Sergio — thanks for the checklist. Quick answers below and I attached our filled inventory.

- Hosts: Rack A: 6 x r730-gpu (NVIDIA A5000), Rack B: 4 x r750-gpu (NVIDIA A100); spare 2 hosts for maintenance.
- Network: All hosts sit behind a top-of-rack switch with a L3 aggregation; there is a rack-level ACL that blocks outbound SSH to internet except through a jump host.
- NVMe: Each GPU host has 2x 3.2TB NVMe drives. Those are currently used for a mix: one drive is host OS and cache, the other is available for tenant-local ephemeral use. We cannot guarantee both drives remain free — ops team reserves the right to use secondary for emergency scratch.
- Retention: Logs: 90 days. Model artifacts: default 180 days, but legal may ask to archive some artifacts for up to 3 years (we'll flag specific models later). No WORM requirement today, but audit logging must be available.

Attaching inventory CSV and a short note from our security team about the jump-host restriction.

Cheers,
Sarah
Sarah Nguyen
Platform Ops, Rackside Labs

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2026 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rackside site intake: node profiles, local NVMe topology & retention constraints

Thanks for the details, Sarah (copying internally). Two immediate flags from product/security:

1) Rackside's jump-host egress constraint means we must validate our private control-plane connectivity flow. We cannot assume direct internet egress from worker nodes for image pulls or telemetry. Need an airgapped artifact fetch plan (registry mirror or pre-pulled images).

2) NVMe uncertainty (ops may reclaim secondary drive) implies we should classify local NVMe as 'non-guaranteed ephemeral' for our scheduling decisions. For model shards and KV cache we can use local NVMe with eviction policies, but user data and artifacts must land in persistent blob (S3-compatible) mounted off-host or on an iSCSI/NAS.

Neha/Priyom: can you draft two node-pool variants:
- Variant A (conservative): GPU workers with 1 local NVMe used only for ephemeral KV/cache; persistent storage in on-site object store (Ceph/S3).
- Variant B (aggressive): GPU workers claim local NVMe for higher-throughput model cache with fallback to blob-store for artifacts; requires periodic sync and integrity checks.

I'll follow up with proposed SLA language for node eviction and artifact sync windows.

- Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Deployment Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 02 Oct 2026 07:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rackside site intake: node profiles, local NVMe topology & retention constraints

On Fri, Oct 1, 2026 at 11:18 AM Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks for the details, Sarah (copying internally). Two immediate flags from product/security:
> ...

Drafting Variant A/B below — high-level numbers only (will produce a one-page decision table).

Variant A (conservative):
- Control plane: 3 x r730 (dedicated, no GPUs) in 3 physical hosts across racks (etcd quorum protected).
- GPU worker pools: 8 x r730-gpu (A5000) + 4 x r750-gpu (A100) as mixed pools; label pools by capability (a5000, a100).
- Local NVMe: Mount as ephemeral scratch via emptyDir: medium=Memory for small files; use hostPath-backed ephemeral for KV with eviction TTL 1 hour.
- Persistent store: Ceph RGW in-rack or MinIO on dedicated hosts with replication to remote object store. Model artifacts written to MinIO; scheduled background sync to S3 bucket in our cloud for long-term archive.
- Retention: model artifacts default 180d; queued archives to cloud at 30d for legal-hold candidates.

Variant B (aggressive throughput):
- Same control plane sizing.
- GPU worker pools: prefer A100s for model serving; assign local NVMe as cache PVs (CSI local PV + nodeAffinity) sized ~2TB per pod, ephemeral eviction with preStop sync to MinIO.
- Requires: pre-seeded registry mirror on jump-host or local registry; image pull policy IfNotPresent.
- Data integrity checks: periodic checksum reconciliation (daily) + alerting for drive reclaim events.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Rack ops reclaims NVMe -> mitigation: enforce writes to MinIO and treat cache as reconstructable; run readiness probes that failover to remote blob.
- Risk: No direct egress -> mitigation: pre-pull or mirror images + relay for telemetry via jump-host.

I'll put a draft decision table and one-page node-pool BOM in the shared Drive link and propose we present to Rackside on Tuesday.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Rackside site intake: node profiles, local NVMe topology & retention constraints

Hi Sarah — thanks again for the fast turn. We've sketched two operational models (conservative & throughput-optimized) and attached the short decision table. Next steps if this looks good to you:

1) Confirm whether you can host a local registry mirror reachable via the jump-host (preferred) or whether we should pre-pull images during deployment windows.
2) Confirm a contact for the rack ops change window (we'll need a 2-hour maintenance window to attach CSI local PVs and test eviction scenarios).
3) Confirm the disposition for the secondary NVMe drive — if ops cannot guarantee availability, we'll recommend Variant A by default.

If you sign off, we'll finalize the node-pool BOM and deliver the preflight checklist by 2026-10-08.

Thanks,
Sergio
